section: Purpose and Scope of the Policy
chunk: The Performance Review & Appraisal Policy aims to establish a structured framework for evaluating employee performance across Global Service Firm. This policy is designed to foster a culture of continuous improvement, align individual contributions with organizational goals, and support employee development. Scope: This policy applies to all employees, including fulltime, parttime, temporary staff, and contractors across all global locations.
Conducted once a year, typically in Q4. Focus on overall performance, achievements, and areas for growth.
Conducted in Q2. A checkpoint to assess progress against goals and adjust as necessary.

Conducted at the end of the probation period (typically 36 months). Assess fit within the team and performance against initial expectations. Example: An employee who joined in January will have their probationary review in June. Feedback will focus on their adaptation to company culture and initial performance metrics.

Exceeds Expectations (5): Consistently surpasses goals. Meets Expectations (4): Achieves all assigned goals. Partially Meets Expectations (3): Meets some goals; needs improvement. Does Not Meet Expectations (2): Fails to meet most goals. Unsatisfactory (1): Consistently underperforms. Example: An employee rated as "Exceeds Expectations" may have led a project that resulted in a 20% increase in client satisfaction.

section: Goal Setting and Alignment with Company Strategy
chunk: Employees will set SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Timebound) goals in alignment with departmental and corporate objectives. Goals should be documented and reviewed during performance discussions. Scenario: An employee in marketing sets a goal to increase social media engagement by 30% over six months, aligning with the company’s strategy to enhance brand visibility.

Managers are encouraged to provide ongoing feedback throughout the year. Regular checkins (monthly or bimonthly) should be scheduled to discuss progress and challenges. Sample Dialogue: Manager: “I noticed your recent presentation was wellreceived. Let’s build on that momentum for the upcoming project.” Employee: “Thank you! I’d love to explore more ways to engage the audience.”
Set personal goals and actively seek feedback. Engage in selfassessment prior to reviews.
Provide regular feedback and conduct formal reviews. Document performance discussions and outcomes.
Facilitate training for managers on performance appraisal processes. Maintain records of performance reviews.
Ensure consistency in ratings across departments. Review performance ratings to mitigate bias.
Performance reviews must be documented using the company’s appraisal form. All feedback and discussions should be recorded in the employee’s HR file.

Performance reviews will identify training needs and career development opportunities. Employees are encouraged to pursue professional development aligned with their career aspirations. Example: An employee identified as needing project management skills may be recommended for a training program.

Performance ratings will directly influence promotion eligibility and compensation adjustments. Employees rated as “Exceeds Expectations” may be considered for leadership roles or salary increases. Scenario: An employee who consistently receives high ratings may be promoted to a senior position, while another with lower ratings may need to improve before being considered for advancement.

Managers should address underperformance immediately with a formal improvement plan. Employees will be given specific goals and a timeline to improve. Example: An employee rated as “Does Not Meet Expectations” will have a 60day plan with weekly checkins to monitor progress.
Employees may appeal their performance ratings within 10 working days of receiving their review. Appeals should be submitted in writing to HR, outlining the reasons for the appeal.
New employees will have a probationary review to assess their fit and performance.
Employees transferring to a new department will undergo a review after 90 days in their new role.
Employees on extended leave will have their reviews postponed until their return.
Schedule review meetings in advance. Prepare documentation and feedback. Discuss goals and performance with the employee. Document the review outcome.

Q1: How often will performance reviews be conducted? A1: Performance reviews are conducted annually, with midyear checkins and probationary reviews for new hires. Q2: Can I appeal my performance rating? A2: Yes, you can appeal your rating within 10 working days by submitting a written request to HR. Q3: What if I disagree with my manager’s feedback? A3: Discuss your concerns with your manager first. If unresolved, you may escalate to HR. Q4: How are goals set? A4: Goals are set collaboratively between the employee and manager, ensuring alignment with company objectives. Q5: What happens if I am underperforming? A5: You will receive a performance improvement plan outlining specific goals and timelines for improvement. Q6: How does this policy affect promotions? A6: Performance ratings directly influence promotion eligibility, with higher ratings increasing your chances. Q7: What documentation is required for reviews? A7: Documentation includes the appraisal form, feedback notes, and any relevant performance data.  This Performance Review & Appraisal Policy is designed to ensure clarity and consistency in assessing employee performance, contributing to a motivated and highperforming workforce at Global Service Firm.
